evidence.note: Read ddflow/api/lifecycle/sync.py (tree_item resolution + _here/called_from), ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py (check_drift stale_rules remedy), ddflow/services/drift.py (item_base), ddflow/surfaces/context.py (called_from / foreign_tree_owner). CONFIRMED: the stale_rules refusal prints a bare 'ddflow sync --keep-local', which relies on tree_item resolving the item from the caller's cwd; a CLI caller whose --agent identity does not match the tree's derived identity is answered from the primary (foreign_tree_owner), so tree_item returns None and sync answers 'this is not an item's worktree'. Regression test test_the_stale_rules_remedy_names_the_item_when_the_tree_is_the_items_worktree fails on the bare command and passes with 'ddflow sync T1 --keep-local'.

Read the work-queue rules (claim before edit, regression test first, cross-family reviewer, unavailable-never-passed) and the drift/tree_owner/sync code; no rule conflicts with naming the item in the remedy.

ddflow/services/drift.py: extracted _tree_item, kept item_base, added item_id; ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py: stale_rules remedy now names the item via _sync_remedy(item_id(...)); tests/test_rulebook_gate.py: regression test. ruff format/check clean; 28 rulebook + 16 sync-command + 22 sync-keep-local tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: When the event log is unreadable in an item worktree, `_tree_item` explicitly catches the exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, so `_sync_remedy` emits the old bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. Because `check_drift` is documented to keep measuring against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, `d.rules` can still be non-empty, so the stale-rules refusal is still produced there. Running the bare remedy from the item's worktree with `--agent` still fails exactly as B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree reports. The fix only fixes the readable-log path, not the explicitly handled unreadable-log path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py item_id / ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py _sync_remedy

chunk_findings.detail: The test docstring promises “the remedy must be a command that WORKS,” but the assertion only checks that `E.check_drift` returns a string containing `"ddflow sync T1 --keep-local"`. It never executes that command in the worktree (for example via `run_cli(repo, "sync", "T1", "--keep-local", cwd=wt)` or the `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` path from B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree). A change that prints the named remedy while the command still fails in the item worktree, or fails under the `--agent` CLI invocation described in the bug, would still pass this test, so the actual regression is not guarded.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rulebook_gate.py:427

chunk_findings.detail: The shared finder dropped the old `it.base` filter that `item_base` used before picking a winner. Given two items whose worktree resolves to the same path — a live item with `base=""` and a finished item with `base="main"` — the live item sorts first (`state in (DONE, ABANDONED)` is false), so `item_base` returns `""` and drift measures against the default branch. Previously only the finished item matched, so the recorded base `"main"` was used. Rule edits that landed only on that base are then not what the stale-rules check compares, and a commit the gate is meant to refuse can pass.

chunk_findings.detail: When the event log cannot be read in an item worktree (for example a corrupt log file), `_tree_item` catches the exception and returns `None`; `item_id` then returns `""`, and `_sync_remedy("")` emits the old bare `    ddflow sync --keep-local`. `check_drift` is documented to keep measuring against the default branch when the item base cannot be read, so `d.rules` can still be non-empty and the stale-rules refusal is still produced there. Running that exact refused remedy from the item's worktree through `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` still fails exactly as reported in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree, because the remedy still does not name the item. The fix only names the item when the event log is readable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:item_id / ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py:_sync_remedy

chunk_findings.detail: The shared `_tree_item` now returns the live item without the old `it.base` filter `item_base` used before choosing a winner. Given a live item with `base==""` and a finished item with `base=="main"` whose stored worktree paths both resolve to `here`, `_tree_item` sorts the live item first, so `item_base` returns `""`; previously the base-bearing finished item matched and `item_base` returned `"main"`. As a result `check_drift` measures against the default branch instead of the recorded base `"main"`, and rule edits that landed only on that recorded base are ignored, so a stale-rules refusal is missed. The new `item_id` wants the live item, but `item_base` needed a base-aware selection.

chunk_findings.detail: The added test only asserts that `E.check_drift(repo, _cfg(), here=wt)` returns a string containing `"ddflow sync T1 --keep-local"`. It never executes that command from the item worktree (for example via `run_cli(repo, "sync", "T1", "--keep-local", cwd=wt)` or the `.ddflow/local/bin/ddflow --agent` path named in B-sync-remedy-not-an-item-worktree). The docstring claims “the remedy must be a command that WORKS,” but the assertion does not verify that; a change that prints the named remedy while the command still fails under the bug’s conditions would pass this regression test. This is the same defect as previous finding 2 and the current diff does not address it.
